Subject: Clarifying purchase lanes for our EU pilot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement had a follow-up: for our EU pilot we need clear guidance on whether to purchase via AWS Marketplace private offer (so accounting remains on our side) or to do a direct purchase (signed MSA + invoice from Redwood). Our compliance team is sensitive to seller-of-record, data residency considerations, and audit evidence for KMS access.

Can you outline the tradeoffs and the simplest path to get us started with a 6-month pilot while keeping the option to convert to a Reserved/Dedicated contract later? Also any timing expectations for a private offer vs. direct contracting would be helpful.

Appreciate a short decision framework we can share with procurement.

Best,
Elena
Procurement Lead, HealthCloud

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the doc. Quick reply with a pragmatic decision tree below; I've also attached a one-page flow diagram for procurement. If you want, we can convert this into a two-line recommendation for your PO owner.

Short summary (TL;DR):
- If you need the vendor to be seller-of-record and want a Marketplace billing footprint (for consolidated AWS procurement), use the AWS Marketplace private offer. It's faster for procurement approval in many customers and supports private pricing.
- If you require a Redwood-issued invoice, specific MSAs with redlines, or SSO/KMS contract terms that we must commit to directly, choose direct contracting (signed MSA + invoice).

Decision factors (how to pick):
1) Seller-of-record / invoicing: Marketplace = AWS is seller-of-record; Direct = Redwood invoices you.
2) Contract redlines / legal terms: Marketplace private offers accept standard marketplace terms — if you need custom MSA clauses (data residency, KMS responsibilities, audit language) go direct.
3) Timing: Marketplace private offer + PO usually 5–10 business days after approval (faster for buyers already using AWS PO flows). Direct MSA + PO can take 2–6 weeks depending on legal review and negotiating redlines.
4) Co-sell / incentives: If you want Redwood + AWS co-sell assistance and channel credits, we can enable co-sell on a private offer; we'll work with our partner manager to register the deal.
5) Future path: Pilot via Marketplace private offer is reversible — you can later convert to a Reserved/Dedicated contract or sign a direct MSA when ready.

Recommended next steps for HealthCloud pilot (simple):
- Option A (fastest): Create a private offer on AWS Marketplace. You raise a PO to AWS once the private offer is accepted. We coordinate with our marketplace ops to set pricing and co-sell registration.
- Option B (controls-first): Start MSA redline + SOW in parallel while running a short private-offer pilot to avoid delay. If legal needs time, pilot continues under the private offer and then we migrate.

I'll loop in Karthik for a short note about KMS/Security evidence and Laura to help with co-sell registration.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk procurement through the two options.

— Soojin
Director, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — adding a few security/compliance specifics to inform the legal decision.

On KMS & data residency:
- Marketplace private offer: you still control customer-side KMS keys (bring-your-own-keys) for encryption at rest if you provision in your cloud account. Redwood does not hold your customer-managed keys for marketplace transactions. You can request SOC2 artifacts and architecture diagrams; we will provide them via our compliance portal.
- Direct contract: we can include contractual language about key management responsibilities, subprocessor lists, and a defined incident response SLA. If your legal needs express obligations, direct contracting makes those promises explicit.

Evidence we can provide immediately for procurement: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), Attestation of Data Processing terms, network architecture diagram, and an exportable audit log sample. If you need a support flow for audit, we can stub a path to provide extracts under NDA.

Operational lead times: marketplace private-offer activation + co-sell registration usually completes within 7 business days once private offer paperwork is accepted. For direct MSA redlines, we typically turn around initial comments in 3 business days but timing depends on complexity of redlines.

If helpful, I can prepare a one-page table mapping their legal questions (from the attached doc) to the recommended lane (Marketplace vs Direct) with suggested contract language.

-Karthik
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that summary is perfect and exactly what procurement wanted. Two quick asks:

1) Can you email the SOC2 redacted PDF and an audit log example under an NDA? Procurement wants a link they can pass to legal.
2) If we go marketplace private offer, can Redwood opt into co-sell registration so we can surface the opportunity to AWS during their internal review?

If both are yes, we'll start a private offer request and circulate a one-page recommendation to the PO approvers.

Best,
Elena
